page.name: Several connected accounts vs one
page.h1: Several connected SMS accounts vs a single provider account
page.metaTitle: Multiple provider accounts vs a single account
page.metaDescription: What a second connected account buys you: failover when one stops accepting traffic, throughput that actually grows, and coverage a single account cannot hold.
page.lede: A single account is a single point of failure you cannot see breaking until customers tell you. Connecting a second turns that into failover you configure once — which is why routing belongs in the layer rather than bolted on later.

sections.h: What a second connected account gives you
bullets: Automatic failover when one account stops accepting traffic — the message moves instead of failing
Throughput that genuinely grows, because pacing is applied per sender number and each account brings its own
Coverage across destinations where a single account cannot hold every identity
One routing decision, configured once, instead of a single default path you hope holds

sections.h: What it takes to hold two accounts well
bullets: Two registrations to keep current — the console keeps them visible rather than hiding them behind one number
Receipts and logs matter more with two accounts, which is why normalization is part of the layer rather than an add-on
Failover only helps when accounts fail independently — two numbers on the same provider is not resilience

p: Start with one account and take it end to end. Add the second when a specific ceiling — a per-number limit, an outage, a destination you cannot reach — is the thing standing in your way. The layer is built so that connecting the second account is the whole change.

faq.q: Is failover available on every channel?
faq.a: Automatic failover between connected accounts ships on the SMS channel today — the channel where a provider-side outage is the failure that costs you messages. Email and WhatsApp carry their own provider-side limits and are handled by those channels.

faq.q: Does more accounts mean less pacing discipline?
faq.a: No — that is the point. Pacing still applies per sender number, so more numbers raise the ceiling rather than removing the limit.

faq.q: Do we need two accounts to use the platform?
faq.a: No. One account is a fully supported setup; the second is there for the day you want failover rather than a single path.
